title: Choose the PULSO cross-portal UI family
question: Each option now shows the full journey from public hero through separate resident and government sign-in to both authenticated workspaces. Choose the family that should become the Figma direction.

options.label: Signal Observatory
options.lineage: city operations observatory and measured signal field
options.thesis: The city appears as a calm living signal, with PULSO translating place into accountable action.
options.viewport: A dark cinematic city horizon spans the hero while a single measured Signal Cut moves through mapped districts; copy and two resident tasks sit quietly in the foreground.
options.risk: The signal field must remain meaningful and restrained or it becomes generic sci-fi decoration.

options.label: Civic Horizon
options.lineage: cinematic city title sequence and public-service monumentality
options.thesis: North Caloocan itself is the hero; PULSO arrives as the clear civic action layer over a composed urban horizon.
options.viewport: A wide architectural city image owns the right two-thirds while a minimal typographic statement and Report / Track actions occupy the left; government access is a separate quiet gate.
options.risk: Weak or generic photography would reduce the direction to a municipal campaign page.

options.label: Living City Atlas
options.lineage: local cartography, transit diagrams, and responsive civic maps
options.thesis: Residents enter through a living map of their city, then choose whether to report, track, or explore verified updates.
options.viewport: A precise Caloocan atlas becomes the hero canvas, with one active Signal Cut and restrained location labels; a compact task dock holds Report, Track, and Resident sign-in.
options.risk: The map must be locally accurate and accessible, not an abstract network graphic.
